Typst is a new markup-based typesetting system that is designed to be as powerful as LaTeX while being much easier to learn and use. Typst has: - Built-in markup for the most common formatting tasks - Flexible functions for everything else - A tightly integrated scripting system - Math typesetting, bibliography management, and more - Fast compile times thanks to incremental compilation - Friendly error messages in case something goes wrong ## Example A [gentle introduction][tutorial] to Typst is available in our documentation. However, if you want to see the power of Typst encapsulated in one image, here it is:

Let's dissect what's going on: - We use _set rules_ to configure element properties like the size of pages or the numbering of headings. By setting the page height to `auto`, it scales to fit the content. Set rules accommodate the most common configurations. If you need full control, you can also use [show rules][show] to completely redefine the appearance of an element. - We insert a heading with the `= Heading` syntax. One equals sign creates a top level heading, two create a subheading and so on. Typst has more lightweight markup like this; see the [syntax] reference for a full list. - [Mathematical equations][math] are enclosed in dollar signs. By adding extra spaces around the contents of an equation, we can put it into a separate block. Multi-letter identifiers are interpreted as Typst definitions and functions unless put into quotes. This way, we don't need backslashes for things like `floor` and `sqrt`. And `phi.alt` applies the `alt` modifier to the `phi` to select a particular symbol variant. - Now, we get to some [scripting]. To input code into a Typst document, we can write a hash followed by an expression. We define two variables and a recursive function to compute the n-th fibonacci number. Then, we display the results in a center-aligned table. The table function takes its cells row-by-row. Therefore, we first pass the formulas `$F_1$` to `$F_8$` and then the computed fibonacci numbers. We apply the spreading operator (`..`) to both because they are arrays and we want to pass the arrays' items as individual arguments.
Text version of the code example. ```typst #set page(width: 10cm, height: auto) #set heading(numbering: "1.") = Fibonacci sequence The Fibonacci sequence is defined through the recurrence relation $F_n = F_(n-1) + F_(n-2)$. You can also watch source files and automatically recompile on changes. This is
faster than compiling from scratch each time because Typst has incremental
compilation.
```sh
# Watches source files and recompiles on changes.
typst watch file.typ
```

Typst further allows you to add custom font paths for your project and list all
of the fonts it discovered:
```sh
# Adds additional directories to search for fonts.
typst compile --font-path path/to/fonts file.typ

# Lists all of the discovered fonts in the system and the given directory.
typst fonts --font-path path/to/fonts

# Or via environment variable (Linux syntax).
TYPST_FONT_PATHS=path/to/fonts typst fonts
```

For other CLI subcommands and options, see below:
```sh
# Prints available subcommands and options.
typst help

# Prints detailed usage of a subcommand.
typst help watch
```

If you prefer an integrated IDE-like experience with autocompletion and instant 
preview, you can also check out our [free web app][app]. Alternatively, there is 
a community-created language server called 
[Tinymist](https://myriad-dreamin.github.io/tinymist/) which is integrated into 
various editor extensions.

## Community
The main places where the community gathers are our [Forum][forum] and our
[Discord server][discord]. The Forum is a great place to ask questions, help
others, and share cool things you created with Typst. The Discord server is more
suitable for quicker questions, discussions, or just to chat.
We'd be happy to see you there!

[Typst Universe][universe] is where the community shares templates and packages.

## Pronunciation and Spelling
IPA: /taɪpst/. "Ty" like in **Ty**pesetting and "pst" like in Hi**pst**er. When
writing about Typst, capitalize its name as a proper noun, with a capital "T".

import struct
def parse(path):
    data=open(path,'rb').read()
    # sfnt header
    num=struct.unpack('>H', data[4:6])[0]
    tables={}
    off=12
    for i in range(num):
        tag=data[off:off+4].decode(); checksum, offset, length=struct.unpack('>III', data[off+4:off+16]); tables[tag]=(offset,length); off+=16
    print(path, tables.keys())
    if 'name' in tables:
        o,l=tables['name']
        fmt,count,stroff=struct.unpack('>HHH', data[o:o+6])
        print(" name count",count)
        for i in range(count):
            platform,encoding,lang,nameId,length,offset=struct.unpack('>HHHHHH', data[o+6+i*12:o+6+i*12+12])
            s=data[o+stroff+offset:o+stroff+offset+length]
            try:
                txt=s.decode('utf-16-be') if platform in (0,3) else s.decode('latin1')
            except: txt=repr(s)
            if nameId in (1,2,4,6,16):
                print(f"  p{platform} e{encoding} l{lang} id{nameId} = {txt!r}")
    if 'OS/2' in tables:
        o,l=tables['OS/2']
        weight=struct.unpack('>H', data[o+4:o+6])[0]
        fsSel=struct.unpack('>H', data[o+62:o+64])[0]
        print(" weight",weight,"fsSel",fsSel, "italic", bool(fsSel&1))
    if 'head' in tables:
        o,l=tables['head']
        mac=struct.unpack('>H', data[o+44:o+46])[0]
        print(" macStyle",mac)
for f in ["DejaVuSans.ttf","DejaVuSans-Bold.ttf","DejaVuSansMono.ttf"]:
    parse(f"/usr/share/fonts/truetype/dejavu/{f}")

# So set gutter_pad = " "*(width+1) for ┌/│/caret lines. Source line stays "{num} │ " but should be right-aligned to width: format!("{:>width$} │ ", num).

            's.push_str(&format!("{} │ {}\\n", format_args!("{:>width$}", line_num_str, width = width), src_line));')

Ref counts from doc start: byte 1.

# Cleanest: give Parser a base_offset added to every token start/end at lex time. Tokens already carry start/end from Lexer over `rest`. Add Parser::new_with_base(src, base) that shifts all token starts/ends by base, and line_col computations inside parser use... parser errors use line_col_of(&self.src, start) where self.src is `rest` — with shifted starts they'd index out of range/wrong.
# Alternative: Diag stores line/col AND we post-adjust: WithErrors carries code_start (byte offset in doc). At diag emission in eval (ident errors etc.), we don't know we're inside hash code...

Since hash code usually starts mid-line, doc_line = line_of(code_start) + (rest_line-1); doc_col = if rest_line==1 { col_of(code_start)+rest_col } else { rest_col }.

    src=os.path.join(d,"w.typ"); outp=os.path.join(d,"w.pdf")

    for label, exe in [("ref",REF),("new",NEW)]:

        time.sleep(1.2)
        exists1=os.path.exists(outp) and open(outp,'rb').read(5)==b"%PDF-"
        mtime1=os.path.getmtime(outp) if os.path.exists(outp) else 0
        open(src,"w").write("Watch v2 longer content")
        time.sleep(1.5)
        mtime2=os.path.getmtime(outp) if os.path.exists(outp) else 0
        p.send_signal(signal.SIGTERM)
        try: p.wait(timeout=3)
        except: p.kill()
        err=p.stderr.read() if p.stderr else b""

        if exists1 and mtime2>mtime1: PASS+=1

        # reset for next impl

fn validate_refs(doc: &MarkupDoc, labels: &[String], source: &str) -> Result<(), Diag> {
    fn walk(nodes: &[Node], labels: &[String], source: &str) -> Result<(), Diag> {
        for n in nodes {
            match n {
                Node::Ref(name, _, s, e) => {
                    if !labels.contains(name) {
                        let (line, col) = crate::diag::line_col_of(source, *s);
                        let len = source[*s..*e].chars().count();
                        return Err(Diag::error_at(format!("label `<{}>` does not exist in the document", name), line, col, len));
                    }
                }
                Node::Strong(b, _) | Node::Emph(b, _) => walk(&b.nodes, labels, source)?,
                Node::Heading(_, b, _, _) => walk(&b.nodes, labels, source)?,
                Node::ListItem(b, _) => walk(&b.nodes, labels, source)?,
                Node::EnumItem(_, b, _) => walk(&b.nodes, labels, source)?,
                Node::TermItem(a, b, _) => { walk(&a.nodes, labels, source)?; walk(&b.nodes, labels, source)?; }
                _ => {}
            }
        }
        Ok(())
    }
    walk(&doc.nodes, labels, source)
}

/// Split evaluated document content into pages of blocks (pagebreak splits pages).
pub fn document_blocks(root: &Content) -> Vec<Vec<BlockItem>> {
    let children = flatten_top(root);
    let mut pages: Vec<Vec<BlockItem>> = vec![Vec::new()];
    let mut cur_para: Vec<InlineItem> = Vec::new();
    let mut cur_list: Vec<Vec<InlineItem>> = Vec::new();
    let mut list_open = false;
    let mut cur_enum: Vec<(i64, Vec<InlineItem>)> = Vec::new();
    let mut enum_open = false;
    let mut enum_next: i64 = 1;
    let flush_para = |pages: &mut Vec<Vec<BlockItem>>, cur: &mut Vec<InlineItem>| {
        let trimmed = trim_items(std::mem::take(cur));
        if !trimmed.is_empty() { pages.last_mut().unwrap().push(BlockItem::Paragraph(trimmed)); }
    };
    let flush_list = |pages: &mut Vec<Vec<BlockItem>>, cur_list: &mut Vec<Vec<InlineItem>>, open: &mut bool| {
        if *open && !cur_list.is_empty() { pages.last_mut().unwrap().push(BlockItem::List(std::mem::take(cur_list))); }
        *open = false;
        cur_list.clear();
    };
    let flush_enum = |pages: &mut Vec<Vec<BlockItem>>, cur_enum: &mut Vec<(i64, Vec<InlineItem>)>, open: &mut bool| {
        if *open && !cur_enum.is_empty() { pages.last_mut().unwrap().push(BlockItem::Enum(std::mem::take(cur_enum))); }
        *open = false;
        cur_enum.clear();
    };
    let numbering: Option<String> = engine.set_styles.iter().filter(|(n,_)| n=="heading").last()
        .and_then(|(_, named)| named.iter().find(|(k,_)| k=="numbering").map(|(_, v)| v.clone()))
        .and_then(|v| if let Value::Str(s)=v { Some(s) } else { None });
    let mut heading_counters: Vec<i64> = Vec::new();
    let heading_show_body = engine.show_rules.iter().any(|(t, _)| t == "heading:body");
    for ch in &children {
        match ch.func.as_str() {
            "parbreak" => { flush_para(&mut pages, &mut cur_para); flush_list(&mut pages, &mut cur_list, &mut list_open); flush_enum(&mut pages, &mut cur_enum, &mut enum_open); enum_next = 1; }
            "pagebreak" => { flush_para(&mut pages, &mut cur_para); flush_list(&mut pages, &mut cur_list, &mut list_open); flush_enum(&mut pages, &mut cur_enum, &mut enum_open); enum_next = 1; pages.push(Vec::new()); }

# Final: commit, rebuild fresh clone incl. this fix, quick regression
git add -A && git -c user.name="Muse Spark" -c user.email="dev@example.invalid" commit -m "Fix TERM/dumb color gating, place mutation, float exponents, and selector field errors" 2>&1 | head -n 4
rm -rf /tmp/freshclone && git clone -q /workspace /tmp/freshclone && cd /tmp/freshclone && ./compile.sh 2>&1 | tail -n 2 && ./executable --version && ./executable eval '{ let a=(1,2); a.push(3); a }'
ln -sf /tmp/freshclone/executable /tmp/cmp/new/executable
python3 /tmp/compare.py 2>&1 | tail -n 2; python3 /tmp/compare2.py 2>&1 | tail -n 2
cd /workspace && git status --porcelain; git log --oneline | head -n 4; ls -la
